sentences.text: Digambar Dhiman vs State Of Uttarakhand on 13 August, 2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 1st Bail Application No. 393 of 2022
Digambar Dhiman ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Sushil Kumar, Advocate for the applicant.
 Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, Aga for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Digambar Dhiman is in judicial custody in FIR/Case Crime No. 93 of 2021, under
Sections 363, 376 Ipc and Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012, Police Station Basant Vihar, District Dehradun.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the victim left her home at 04:30 a.m. on 21.05.2021.
The FIR was lodged by the father of the victim.
According to the prosecution, subsequently, the victim was recovered when she was with the applicant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant and the victim both were in relationship; when the victim was recovered, she revealed to the police that she was in romantic relationship with the applicant for the last five years; since her family members were not agreeable to it, they wanted to get her married to some other person, but the victim wanted to marry the applicant, therefore, she left the house on 21.05.2021.
Reference has been made to the recovery memo, which is filed along with the supplementary affidavit.

5. Learned State Counsel admits that initially the victim has stated that she was in relationship with the applicant, but in her subsequent statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, she has stated that the applicant would follow her, took her along with him and established physical relations with her.
The victim has been examined at trial.
6. It is the stage of bail.
Much of the discussion is not expected of.
The discussion is being made with a caveat that any observation made in this order should not have any bearing at trial.

7. At the initial stage, when the victim was recovered, she revealed to the police that she was in romantic relationship with the applicant for the last five years and since her family members were not agreeable to it and she wanted to marry the applicant, she left her house.
Subsequently, the victim changed her statement, but still she maintains that the applicant was known to her.

8. In the cases of Mahesh Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine Del 2634, Faizan Wahid Baig v. The State of Maharashtra, MANU/MHOR/62774/2022, Vijaylakshmi and another v. State and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Mad 317, Shri John Franklin Shylla v. State of Meghalaya & Anr.,
2023 SCC OnLine Megh 303 and Ashik Ramjali Ansari v. State of Maharashtra and another, 2023 SCC OnLine Bom 1390, the Courts have either granted bail or quashed the proceedings or acquitted the accused in the cases like instant one.

sentences.text: 9. Having considered, this Court is of the view that subject to certain conditions, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
10. The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant or any of his relatives shall not make any contact with the victim, in any manner, whatsoever, either physically, electronically or by any other means.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to Court or any Police Officer and the applicant should not tamper with evidence.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 13.08.2024 Avneet/
